purpose: Resolve whether batching six independent virtual-state queries materially changes GRASP runtime, while measuring numerical and gradient differences. This is a cached-input performance probe, not a Clean task, security experiment, or authorization to change the existing task budget.
precision: FP32, frozen model parameters; original input gradients retained

resource.timing_scope: 60 seconds starts before heavy imports, includes local checkpoint loading, all compute and result recording. SIGALRM is best effort during native CUDA work; boundary checks and any overrun are recorded. No retries or backend fallback.

comparison.order: Each fixed stage: six native B1/T1 calls, then one B6/T1 call; no warmup, tuning, repeats or state updates.
comparison.loss: Use official _compute_grasp_loss unchanged for native; batch only independent detached inputs, retain original per-time means and sequential Python sums for dynamics and scheduled goal shaping.
comparison.tolerance_scope: Descriptive fixed allclose checks only. Approximate equality does not establish complete optimizer trajectory or task equivalence. Bitwise equality is reported separately.

sync.method: Invoke the unchanged native _sync_step three times from the same cached stage50 actions, temporarily gd_opt_steps=1. Each call includes one H6 autoregressive rollout, native terminal visual MSE backward, and its fresh Adam update. These are three timing measurements, not a shortened task planner.
sync.optimization: Three input-action updates in isolated discarded clones; zero neural weight updates.
sync.estimate: three_root_planning_seconds = 3 * (37 / 6) * (500 * mean_batched_loss_forward_backward_seconds + 500 * mean_native_H6_sync_update_seconds). Add observed prior setup/load overhead separately and show assumptions/range. No inference that the full task will fit1200seconds from an estimate alone.

stop_rule: Any activity, time, memory, nonfinite, input-integrity or RNG failure stops this one attempt and preserves partial evidence. No automatic rerun, model intervention, task launch, optimizer-step reduction or task budget increase.
